sources.citation: Schmidt, Christopher K. 2013 [degree May 2014]. Morphosyntax of Wangka, a dialect of Rembong-Riung. PhD dissertation, Rice University, xx+299 pp. hdl:1911/103420
sources.note: Ch. 3 Phonology (pp. 93-112) never states where stress falls. Only incidental mentions: p. 97 'In stressed position, a glottalised vowel at final position can be produced as a full glottal stop'; p. 104 glottalisation 'often is weakened or does not occur when the word is not stressed'; p. 108 announces a discussion of 'whether Wangka has phonemic stress, and analyse its basic prosodic patterns' but secs. 3.3.1-3.3.2 (pp. 108-112) cover only syllable structure, clitics and Malay loanword adaptation; no prosody subsection exists (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/pitch/intonation). Vo…
No phonology; only cites Ethnologue and Schmidt 2013 (hdl 1911/103420).

sources.citation: Pita, Petrus; Mbete, Aron Meko; Lauder, Multamia R.M.T; Dhanawaty, Ni Made. 2016. The linguistic status of isolects in Nagekeo regency: a dialect geography analysis. e-Journal of Linguistics (Program Studi Linguistik, Pascasarjana Universitas Udayana) 10(2), July 2016: 100-138. ISSN 2442-7586.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: The phonological component is explicitly restricted to segmental phonemes (p. 105) -- vowel/consonant inventory of Nage-Keo (p. 113), six rule-governed consonant correspondences across the Nagekeo, Mbay/Riung and Ende areas (pp. 113-123), assimilation/prothesis/aphaeresis (pp. 123-126). A a full-text search for stress/accent the full 39-page text finds no occurrence of tone, tonal, stress, pitch, accent, prosody, suprasegmental, intonation, tekanan or nada.

tone.quote: According to Mashun (1995:23) phonological variations or phonological differences are the variations which are related to phonetic differences. The description of variations or differences in linguistic items at phonological level which become the object of analysis in this research focuses on the differences of segmental phonemes.
